Performers
Sergei Rachmaninoff (piano) Documented

The source item, reissue register and Victor matrix record agree on the pianist.

[2] [4] [5]
Work version
Unknown Unknown

Original solo-piano work; the performing edition and any unnotated changes are not identified. The score used for commentary is not asserted to be the copy used at the session.

[2] [4]
Recorded
1921-01-21 Documented

The filename date is independently corroborated by the reissue register and DAHR’s approved take; it is not an upload or CD release date.

[2] [4] [5]
Place
Camden, New Jersey Documented

DAHR specifies Camden for take 5 but no venue. The Church Building Laboratory named for earlier rejected takes is not automatically assigned to the issued take.

[5]
Label
Victor; RCA/BMG reissue Documented

Victor identifies the original commercial issue; the uploader identifies the later RCA/BMG CD set as its immediate source.

[5] [2] [4]
Catalogue
Victor 64963 (10-inch); RCA-BMG 09026 61265 2, CD 10 (1992) Documented

The Victor number and CD set are separately documented. The physical disc transferred for the 1992 mastering is not identified.

[5] [2] [4]
Matrix, take, sides
B-24642-5; one issued side Inferred, not documented

DAHR documents this approved matrix/take and the RCA booklet names it for the reissued track. Its linkage to the current digital file follows the uploader’s stated CD provenance and matching work/date, not an independent waveform or run-out comparison.

[4] [5] [2]
Transfer
John Pfeiffer, reissue producer; Ward Marston, disc-to-DAT transfer; André Gauthier, remastering supervisor; Anthony Salvatore, remastering engineer Documented

These are the original 1992 set’s credits. Their connection to the current access file follows the uploader’s identification of that set; the later ripper/uploader is not named as a mastering engineer.

[4] [2]
Transfer date
Unknown Unknown

The set was issued in 1992, but the date of the disc-to-DAT transfer and the later CD extraction are not stated. The Archive upload occurred in 2025 and is not a transfer-session date.

[4] [2]
Processing
Disc-to-DAT transfer, followed by digital remastering at BMG/RCA Studios, New York City; Archive derives its VBR MP3 from an uploaded WAV. Documented

The booklet says surface imperfections were reduced without radical removal of all surface noise. It does not give equalisation, pitch-correction, noise-reduction or editing settings. No such settings are inferred from the audio analysis.

[4] [3]
Composition rights
Underlying composition is out of copyright where the ordinary life-plus-70 term applies. Inferred, not documented

Rachmaninoff died in 1943. This is a territorial term calculation, not worldwide clearance or a statement about an unidentified modern performing edition.

[8] [9]
Recording rights
US public domain: the issued sound recording was commercially available by 1925; Internet Archive also applies Public Domain Mark 1.0 to the access file. Documented

Victor’s contemporary 1925 catalogue lists this Prelude on record 812, which DAHR maps to the same B-24642 take 5 as the earlier single-faced 64963. This establishes publication no later than 1925, independently of the 1921 session date, and eligibility under the project’s pre-1926 US recording rule. The exact first-publication day remains unknown. The 1992 booklet retains an all-rights-reserved reissue notice: no claim is made that its text, artwork or compilation is public domain, or that any unidentified new creative contribution to the mastering is independently cleared worldwide.

Sergei Rachmaninoff, piano — Victor 64963, matrix B-24642-5. Digital source: RCA/BMG Complete Recordings (1992), CD 10, via Internet Archive; Public Domain Mark 1.0 is the item’s recording-rights statement. Rights statement

Red Seal section, “The Rachmaninoff Records—Continued”: Op. 23 No. 5 and Op. 32 No. 5 both on 6261; Op. 32 No. 12 on 812. Contemporary publication evidence, linked to takes through DAHR.. Accessed 2026-10-17.
  2. Internet Archive: Complete Rachmaninoff, CD 10 — Uploader identifies RCA-BMG 09026 61265 2 (1992), CD 10; selected filenames state individual recording dates; item links the original booklet and Public Domain Mark 1.0.. Accessed 2026-10-17.
  3. Internet Archive item metadata and file manifest — Track-specific WAV originals and generated VBR MP3 access files, durations and licence URL; 2025 upload dates are not session dates.. Accessed 2026-10-17.
  4. RCA: Sergei Rachmaninoff, The Complete Recordings, 10-CD booklet (1992) — Printed p. 20: reissue/transfer credits; essays “The Composer” and “The Recordings”; discographic register pp. 70–⁠71: dates and matrices of the three selected preludes; closing remastering and rights notice. OCR consulted against the named track register.. Accessed 2026-10-17.
  5. DAHR: Victor matrix B-24642-5 — Take table: performer, date, place, master status, original issue and later reissues.. Accessed 2026-10-17.
  6. Gutheil first edition (1911): Thirteen Preludes, Op. 32 — No. 12, printed pp. 48–⁠51.. Accessed 2026-10-17.
  7. U.S. Copyright Office: Classics Protection and Access Act — Term section: recordings first published before 1923 ceased receiving the stated remedies on 31 December 2021; later historic publication periods have different terms.. Accessed 2026-10-17.
  8. IMSLP: Sergei Rachmaninoff — Life dates: 1 April 1873–⁠28 March 1943.. Accessed 2026-10-17.
  9. Directive 2006/116/EC — Articles 1(1) and 8: ordinary life-plus-70 author term, calculated from the following 1 January.. Accessed 2026-10-17.
